analysis.title: US Labour Market: Stubbornly Soft
key_insights: September US non-farm payrolls rose 29,000 m/m versus consensus of 90,000, and the unemployment rate rose unexpectedly.
Strong US growth has not produced any material pickup in labour demand, which reduces the likelihood of domestic price pressures building.
Investors pared back interest rate hike bets and reversed much of the rise in US Treasury yields seen earlier in the week.
Annual non-farm payroll growth is 0.2% y/y, well below trend. The household survey shows employment down 0.3% y/y.
The unemployment rate rose from 4.14% to 4.18% even though immigration enforcement is shrinking the available labour pool.
Hourly earnings growth cooled from 3.1% y/y to 3.0% y/y in September, below August CPI inflation of 3.4%. Higher fuel prices will keep real household spending power falling in Q4.

The August US goods trade deficit was its widest since the start of 2025. Berenberg sees the trade deficit rising from an annualised 3.6% of GDP in Q2 to 4.6% in Q3, as AI infrastructure hardware is imported from Asia and offsets the investment boost to growth.
Berenberg expects the Fed to tighten less than the market prices. The market prices almost three more 25bp hikes, while Berenberg expects one.

If central banks signal a pause in hikes early next year, Berenberg sees bond yields declining slightly. The relief is likely temporary, as slower GDP growth will raise questions about the US government's ability to service its debt.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Far below the 90k consensus, which weakens the case for a fresh round of Fed hikes.
The print missed consensus by about 61,000.
Well below the historical trend rate, showing very weak hiring.
A weaker read than the payrolls survey.
The rate rose despite a shrinking labour pool from immigration enforcement, which points to soft labour demand.
Wage growth is below CPI inflation, so real incomes are falling.
Inflation is running above wage growth, which squeezes household budgets.

macro_indicators.reading: Berenberg expects 1 more 25bp hike, market prices almost 3
macro_indicators.interpretation: Berenberg sees the market overpricing Fed tightening.

risk_factors: Falling real household spending power could slow consumer spending growth.
If consumer spending slows, the AI investment boom is unlikely to offset it.
A widening goods trade deficit from AI hardware imports offsets the investment boost to growth.
Consumer confidence fell in September (Conference Board), which suggests spending may soon slow.
Slower GDP growth raises questions about the US government's ability to service its debt, which could lift borrowing costs again.
vol_and_positioning: Investors pared back bets on interest rate hikes after the payrolls report and reversed much of the week's rise in US Treasury yields.
The market still prices in almost three more 25bp Fed hikes, versus Berenberg's call for one.
geopolitical: President Trump's immigration crackdown is shrinking the pool of available US labour.
Higher fuel prices are reducing real household spending power.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong consumer spending will likely produce another quarter of solid Q3 growth, and survey measures of activity are surging.
tension_points.bear_case: Hiring is very weak, real incomes are falling and the trade deficit is widening, so the expansion rests on shaky foundations. Slowing consumer spending would not be offset by AI investment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A drop in consumer spending growth, as the fall in Conference Board consumer confidence in September suggests may come soon, would confirm the bear case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Weak labour demand reduces the chance of domestic price pressures building, so the Fed will not need to tighten as much as the market prices.
